# Question topic program

Planning date 2026-11-11. Owner direction from Melissa Rowland, surgery resident and named clinical sign-off.

This original editorial taxonomy covers the domains requested by the owner. Priority estimates express expected general-surgery testing relevance and audit urgency. The topic workers will establish their ranked concept lists through permitted-source research. The taxonomy uses independently written scope boundaries.

Each scope includes its relevant anatomy, embryology, physiology, pathology, diagnostic interpretation, operative technique, treatment, complications and follow-up. Technical and scientific objectives retain the owner of their scored organ or cross-cutting construct.

The snapshot uses ship manifest `question-ship.2026-11-10.v9` and the actual exported `SYNTHETIC_CLINICAL_RELEASE`. Capture time is `2026-11-11T15:28:05.732Z`. The JSON companion contains source hashes, identity indexes, hold records and the complete machine-readable census.

The requested 610 total is the registered identity count. Active topic coverage uses the 454 concepts actually attached to live nodes. The retained registry includes older versions and compatibility definitions. Every registered concept receives a primary topic in the JSON concept index.

Live accepted means an exact projected tuple with a manager acceptance row. Live original means a projected carry-forward tuple. These admission labels retain their separate clinical review metadata. Draft parked includes retained historical revisions and source-only variants as well as explicit parks. The retention field identifies that form. An explicit owner-decision hold receives held for owner.

Draft counts measure retained audit rows. They include multiple versions of the same meaning and historical case occurrences of identities that can remain live in another context. The JSON also reports distinct draft variants and concepts, explicit owner-held versions and unassembled variants. Null case, node or complaint fields preserve absent source bindings. Unkeyed slots and withheld teaching points have their own ledgers below.

Zero active clinical identities signals absent coverage. One to four signals thin coverage for wave triage. Larger totals still need a breadth and redundancy audit. Six synthetic engine tutorial identities are included in the census and excluded from clinical breadth. Research agendas identify candidate gaps to investigate.

### Esophagus — motility and achalasia

Stable slug `esophagus-motility-achalasia`. Priority high. Wave 3.

Included scope covers motor physiology, manometry interpretation and adequacy, achalasia, junction outflow disorders, motility-directed treatment and post-treatment failure.

Reflux and Barrett pathways belong to esophagus-gerd-barrett-hiatal. Structural dysphagia, EoE and diverticula belong to esophagus-structural-inflammatory-emergencies.

Common foregut decision chains support both diagnostic interpretation and procedure selection.

At most four distinct live clinical concept identities cover this scope. Variants repeat those identities. The census has 4 live concepts, 8 live nodes and 47 retained draft rows.

#### Research agenda

- Primary versus secondary outflow obstruction.
- Motor-pattern interpretation linked to a specific treatment.
- Treatment failure and competing reflux or mechanical causes.

### Esophagus — GERD, Barrett and hiatal hernia

Stable slug `esophagus-gerd-barrett-hiatal`. Priority high. Wave 3.

Included scope covers reflux confirmation, reflux-test interpretation, antireflux assessment, hiatal/paraesophageal hernia and Barrett dysplasia, surveillance and treatment selection.

A standalone motor-disorder objective belongs to esophagus-motility-achalasia. Esophageal malignancy beyond the Barrett pathway belongs to esophagus-structural-inflammatory-emergencies.

Frequent foregut care combines objective testing with consequential treatment boundaries.

At most four distinct live clinical concept identities cover this scope. Variants repeat those identities. The census has 4 live concepts, 14 live nodes and 1 retained draft row.

#### Research agenda

- Reflux evidence before invasive treatment.
- Paraesophageal hernia complications and operative planning.
- Barrett dysplasia confirmation and stage-appropriate therapy.

## Five-worker waves

The sequence sorts testing priority first and live concept breadth second. Absent and thin topics lead each priority tier. Statistics leads the partial-coverage high-priority group because of the explicit owner-directed repair. Within the remaining group, lower live concept counts and then lower node counts lead. Counts describe structure, and each worker must judge item quality.

### File ownership

The 300 concrete future paths in JSON `taxonomy[].workerLane` and `waves[].lanes` are pairwise distinct. Each wave has exactly five workers, and each worker has five owned paths. The current path check found 0 pre-existing target files. The manager should repeat that existence check before dispatch.

Each topic worker owns the following path pattern with its stable slug substituted.

```text
packages/clinical-content/src/question-topic-<slug>-20261111.ts
packages/clinical-content/src/question-topic-<slug>-20261111.test.ts
docs/research/question-topic-<slug>-20261111.json
docs/research/question-topic-<slug>-20261111.md
docs/research/sources-question-topic-<slug>-20261111.json
```

Existing source files are shared read-only audit inputs. Several contain questions assigned to several topics. All proposals are additive in the worker lane. The manager owns composition into shared source, timing, registries, runtime and the ship manifest after review. This establishes disjoint write lanes for each five-worker wave.

Node and concept ownership follows the scored objective. Each case/header has one primary owner, chosen from its live-node majority with an alphabetical tie-breaker. Retained-only case ownership uses its retained rows. The JSON case index records secondary topics and all node/variant references. Workers inspect complete visible sequences and report cross-topic dependencies through the manager.

Six node IDs are reused across retained versions with different topic constructs. The canonical node index has one live-preferred primary owner. The case/node/variant/concept inventory keeps the version-specific construct owner and links the same node ID. Those cross-version records require manager composition review.

## Biggest coverage gaps

- **Critical care — renal injury and organ support** has 0 live concepts. Investigate oliguria differential and physiology-directed response, renal replacement indication and modality constraints, abdominal compartment assessment and intervention.
- **Critical care — shock and resuscitation** has 0 live concepts. Investigate hemodynamic patterns and treatment response, resuscitation endpoints and competing shock mechanisms, vasoactive/support decisions linked to raw findings.
- **Trauma — initial assessment and abdominal injury** has 0 live concepts. Investigate physiology-directed imaging versus operation, solid-organ and hollow-viscus injury pathways, damage-control and re-exploration decisions.
- **Appendix — appendicitis and appendiceal lesions** has 2 live concepts and 8 nodes. Investigate complicated appendicitis and interval decisions.
- **Small bowel — obstruction and ileus** has 2 live concepts and 8 nodes. Investigate nonoperative eligibility and failure.
- **Trauma — thoracic injury** has 2 live concepts and 8 nodes. Investigate chest drainage, retained blood and operative escalation.
- **Critical care — respiratory failure and ventilation** has 3 live concepts and 12 nodes. Investigate pressure/waveform changes and ventilator action.
- **Pancreas — chronic disease, cysts and tumors** has 3 live concepts and 12 nodes. Investigate cyst phenotype and management-changing findings.
- **Vascular — aortic and peripheral aneurysms** has 3 live concepts and 12 nodes. Investigate rupture and emergency repair strategy.
- **Liver — primary tumors and metastases** has 3 live concepts and 17 nodes. Investigate metastatic liver disease resectability.
- **Esophagus — motility and achalasia** has 4 live concepts and 8 nodes. Investigate primary versus secondary outflow obstruction.
- **Esophagus — GERD, Barrett and hiatal hernia** has 4 live concepts and 14 nodes. Investigate reflux evidence before invasive treatment.
- **Infection — surgical source control and antibiotics** has 4 live concepts and 15 nodes. Investigate anatomical source and drainage route.
- **Colon — diverticular disease and lower GI bleeding** has 4 live concepts and 16 nodes. Investigate abscess, perforation and operative reconstruction.

- **Burns — thermal injury and inhalation** has 3 live concepts and 9 nodes. Investigate inhalation and special-mechanism injury.
- **Vascular — carotid and cerebrovascular disease** has 3 live concepts and 9 nodes. Investigate symptom territory and bilateral disease.

- **Bariatric — selection, anatomy and complications** has 3 live concepts and 12 nodes. Investigate procedure anatomy and acute postoperative emergencies.

## Reusable worker contract

Use [the topic-worker brief template](question-topic-worker-brief-template-20261111.md). The manager fills the scope, exact census record IDs, source/approval holds and five output paths for one topic. Each worker researches a ranked concept list, audits every assigned existing variant, proposes keep/rewrite/retire-and-replace decisions, writes supported revisions and fills high-value gaps. Natural clinical multi-decision cases are preferred. Statistics retains the superseding minimal single-skill format.

The manager performs independent review, exact acceptance and shared integration. The owner supplies clinical sign-off. Worker self-checks and passing tests retain their distinct validation roles.
